summary: Stale portfolio balances come from aa-sync saturating its DB connection pool. Pool use rose from about 22 to 61 at 12:50 and then stayed at 100, and the error rate rose from 0.004 to 0.354 over the same period. portfolio-consumer calls aa-sync (weight 0.8) and consumes the portfolio-updates queue. Its errors rose and the queue consume rate dropped from about 49/s to about 8/s, so the queue backed up to a depth of about 1000 while publishing continued. portfolio-svc is healthy, and the only changes in the window (msg-delivery 12:23, web-app 13:00) do not fit the onset. What started the pool exhaustion is not established: it is either a postgres or query slowdown on holdings_snapshot, or an aa-sync connection leak or load issue, and postgres was not examined.

hypotheses.statement: aa-sync database connection pool exhaustion is the fault point. Its requests queue and error, portfolio-consumer's calls to aa-sync fail, portfolio-updates consumption collapses, and balances go stale.
hypotheses.label: high

supporting.text: aa-sync pool_in_use jumped at 12:50, after a flat baseline of about 22
aa-sync err_rate rose at the same time as the pool filled
portfolio-updates consume_rate started falling at 12:50 from about 49/s
First pool exhaustion error in aa-sync logs at 12:50:08
portfolio-consumer calls aa-sync and aa-sync publishes to portfolio-updates, so failures flow from aa-sync to the consumer
portfolio-updates queue depth reached about 1000 (backlog consequence)

contradicting.text: The log text says pool exhausted at 35/100 in use, while the metric shows about 22 before 12:50 and 61 at 12:50. The two disagree slightly; the metric is preferred for sizing.

hypotheses.statement: A postgres or holdings_snapshot query slowdown (or an aa-sync connection leak) holds connections longer and triggered the pool saturation. This is unverified because postgres was not queried and the slow queries may be a consequence of saturation.
hypotheses.label: low

supporting.text: holdings_snapshot queries slowed progressively while the pool filled (171ms to 400ms)

hypotheses.statement: The web-app deploy on the holdings page caused the incident.
hypotheses.label: low

contradicting.text: Only changes in the window are a log-level tweak at 12:23 and a UI copy change at 13:00 (after onset); none touched aa-sync
portfolio-svc was healthy throughout, so it is not the fault point

assumptions.text: The log text says pool exhausted at 35/100 in use, while the metric shows about 22 before 12:50 and 61 at 12:50. The two disagree slightly; the metric is preferred for sizing.

unresolved: What triggered the pool saturation at about 12:50: postgres slowness, a connection leak, a traffic or consent-refresh spike, or something else. No aa-sync change was found, and postgres metrics and logs were not examined.
The aa-sync WARN/ERROR log query was truncated (251 matches, only the first 30 seen up to 12:53), so later behaviour is known only from metrics.
The logged '35/100 in use' for 'exhausted' disagrees with the metric baseline of about 22 and 61 at 12:50.
portfolio-consumer logs were not inspected to confirm that its errors are aa-sync call failures.

actions.text: Mitigate aa-sync: restart or scale out the instances to release the pool, and temporarily raise the pool size or shed load if safe. Watch pool_in_use and err_rate recover.
actions.rationale: The pool has been pinned at 100 since 12:55 and drives the errors that block portfolio-consumer.

actions.text: Check postgres (active connections, locks, long-running queries on holdings_snapshot) and aa-sync connection handling, to find what started the saturation at about 12:50.
actions.rationale: Slow holdings_snapshot queries preceded or accompanied the pool filling, and postgres has not been examined.

actions.text: After aa-sync recovers, confirm portfolio-updates drains (depth falling from about 1000, redeliveries normal) and no messages are lost or duplicated.
actions.rationale: The queue backlog and elevated redeliveries are consequences that will linger.

actions.text: Add alerting on aa-sync pool_in_use and review pool sizing and timeouts. Fix the log message so it reports the real pool counts.
actions.rationale: The log reported exhaustion at 35/100 while the metric showed different values, and earlier detection would have shortened the impact.
